div.head: Wi 12[a]
div.ab: Gif ceorl buton wifes wisdome deoflum gelde, he sie ealra his æhtan scyldig ⁊ healsfange.
Gif ceorl buton wifes wisdome deoflum gelde, he sie ealra his æhtan scyldig ⁊ healsfange.
Gif ceorl buton wifes wisdome deoflum gelde, he sie ealra his æhtan scyldig ⁊ healsfange.
Wenn ein Ehemann ohne Wissen seiner Frau Götzen opfert, sei er [dem König] all seine [Fahr]habe schuldig und Halsfang.
If a husband sacrifices to idols without his wife’s knowledge, let him be liable [to the king] for all his [movable] goods and his healsfang.
If a husband, without his wife’s knowledge, makes offerings to devils, he shall forfeit all his goods or his healsfang.

If a husband sacrifice to devils without his wife’s knowledge, he is to be liable to pay all his goods and healsfang; if they both sacrifice to devils, they are to be liable to pay healsfang and all their goods.
If a freeman without his wife’s knowledge makes offering to devils, he shall be liable for all his possessions or healsfang.

note.label: another instance
note.quote: For another instance of the separate culpability of husband and wife see Wihtred §9 [L12].

note.seg: Ein ‘Freier’ ist zwar, laut des Gegensatzes zum Sklaven in Wi 13, auch gemeint, aber ein Ehemann laut des folgenden wif. Dass ein Gemeinfreier im Ggs. zum Adel gemeint sei, und dass also Heidentum unter höheren Klassen nicht mehr vorkam, braucht deshalb nicht herausgelesen zu werden. Offenbar wird ein Heide mit einer Christin, nicht ein Christ mit einer Heidin verheiratet gedacht; vgl. Gl Bekehrung 3a

A ‘freeman’ is indeed also meant, given the contrast with the slave in Wi 13, but a husband, given the following wif. It need not therefore be inferred that a common freeman, as opposed to the nobility, is meant, and thus that heathenism no longer occurred among the higher classes. Evidently a heathen husband is envisaged as married to a Christian wife, not a Christian husband to a heathen wife; cf. Gl Bekehrung 3a

‘Teufel’ lebendiger Kraft sah zwar frühes Christentum in den Göttern der Heiden. Doch braucht dieser Aberglaube nicht überall vorzuliegen, wo das Wort deofol steht; dies kann ‘Götze’ heissen (s. Wb: deofolgield), ohne dass Sprechender diesen als wirklich betrachtete

Early Christianity did indeed see in the gods of the heathen ‘devils’ of living power. But this superstition need not be present wherever the word deofol occurs; it can mean ‘idol’ (see Wb: deofolgield) without the speaker regarding the idol as real
Vgl. Gl Heidentum 4f. Schmid meint, vielleicht in Wi 12—15 Spuren von Earconberht zu finden; s. o. S. 17²
Cf. Gl Heidentum 4f. Schmid thinks that traces of Earconberht may perhaps be found in Wi 12—15; see above p. 17²

Der Gen. pl. æhtan ist spät. Vom Einen scyldig hängen zwei verschiedene Casus ab. — Vgl. Gl Vermögenseinziehung 711 Sp. 3 Z. 1. Im Halsfang (s. d. Gl 7) sieht Ersatz der Todesstrafe Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 182, wogegen u. 14 spricht

The gen. pl. æhtan is late. Two different cases depend on the single scyldig. — Cf. Gl Vermögenseinziehung 711 col. 3 l. 1. Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 182 sees in the healsfang (see that word in Gl 7) a substitute for the death penalty, which 14 below contradicts

note.label: or
note.seg: Here and in the next clause, Whitelock takes ⁊ as ‘or.’ Although the meaning of ‘and’ is more common, ⁊ appears elsewhere with adversative meaning in the Kentish laws. See e.g., Æbt §§15, 30, and 80, and compare the previous clause. If the possessions were forfeit anyway, one would have nothing with which to pay healsfang.
